lesson.menu_title: Passive Voice: Professional and Technical Contexts
lesson.menu_desc: Write and say technical updates the way IT reports do: the passive voice (is / are + past participle, was / were + past participle, and by + the agent when it matters) — for the patch report Daniela presents to the US team: a bug was detected, a patch was released, the servers were restored.
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 — Passive Voice: Professional and Technical Contexts
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Daniela Feitoza | Lesson 23 -- Passive Voice: Professional and Technical Contexts
lesson.grammar_point: passive voice (present simple and past simple passive, by + agent)

listenings.text: Hi Daniela, it is Sarah, your English coach. Next week you are going to send your first technical report to the US team, so let us talk about the passive voice. In a technical report, the important thing is usually the action or the result, not the person. So we do not say: somebody detected a bug. We say: a bug was detected. We do not say: Carlos restored the server. We say: the server was restored. For the past, use was or were plus the past participle. The patch was released on Tuesday. The servers were restored at six. For things that happen every day or every week, use is or are. The data is backed up every night. New tickets are assigned to a team. And when the person is important, add by. The patch was approved by the security team. That way, the reader knows who is responsible. One last tip: keep the sentences short. One action per sentence. Your report will be clear, and nobody will feel blamed. Good luck with the report, Daniela.

Hi Daniela, it is Greg. Quick update before the status call. The checkout problem in the US stores is solved. Here is what happened. On Friday, a bug was found in the payment page. It was detected by our monitoring tool at about nine p.m., and it was reported to my team right away. The fix was written on Saturday, and the patch was tested by the QA team on Sunday morning. It was approved by the security team at noon, and it was released at two p.m. All the servers were restored by six. No customer data was lost. Now, the important part. The same system is used in the Brazilian stores, so the patch needs to be installed there too. Could you include this in your report for the call? Thanks, Daniela. Talk soon.

extra_audio.text: First, a bug was found in the payment page on Friday night. Then it was reported to Greg's team, and a fix was written on Saturday. After that, the patch was tested by the QA team on Sunday morning. Next, it was approved by the security team and released at two p.m. Finally, all the servers were restored, and the patch was installed in the Brazilian stores.
